- **On behalf of my co-authors, Brian Falcone, PhD Elvira Dsouza and Renu Juneja, PhD , I am proud to share the publication of the second Medical Affairs Professional Society (MAPS) white paper on Integrated Medical Communications (iMC) — a practical “how-to” guide that builds on the original concept paper we published a few years ago. https://lnkd.in/e-BMWh2k Both position papers reflect work we’ve been deeply invested in over time: helping Medical Affairs organizations advance medical strategy via integrated, consistent and credible scientific story-telling across deliverables and communication platforms. Multiple organizations have since adopted this approach. What continues to matter most is that integrated Medical Communications intentionally connects insight, evidence, and narrative so that strong medical strategy is consistently reflected across publications, medical education, stakeholder engagement, and external scientific exchange. When done well, Integrated Medical Communications -Creates shared ownership with Medical Strategy for how evidence is generated, interpreted, and communicated – both functions are strategically connected, not sequential -Enables clearer, more durable and repeatable scientific narratives across all communication platforms, internal and external -Strengthens cross-functional alignment while preserving scientific rigor, compliance, and trust Medical Communications, when integrated early and intentionally, becomes a powerful partner in Medical Affairs teams –and elevates how Medical Affairs shows up — not as a series of disconnected activities, but as a strategically aligned system that supports better decision-making and ultimately better patient outcomes. This work was a true collaboration, and I’m grateful to my co-authors and the MAPS Medical Communications Functional Area Working Group that was a true Think Tank, and contributed their thinking and insights, reviewed drafts, and helped sharpen this practical guidance. ( Avishek Pal , Clare Baker , Elise Blankenship, PhD, CMPP Ezinneka Imoh, PharmD , Fran Paradiso-Hardy , Marleen van der Voort, MD , Narmada Rosner, MBA, MSc , Paolo Marchi, Paul O'Grady , Sissy Easo-Joseph, MS, PhD and Teri Michelini — Thank you all). Thank you Garth Sundem for all your support and help throughout the process! You can access hands-on training on developing an iMC through regularly scheduled MAPS MasterClasses or through a customized MasterClass Onsite program for your organization (contact Peter Piliero ). - **After almost 20 years, tomorrow will be my last day at Astellas Pharma . As Maya Angelou said, “Every journey begins with a single step.” Looking back, I could never have imagined where that first step would lead. Throughout my time at Astellas, I have had the privilege of leading transformational change across affiliate, sub-regional, and global levels. Together, we challenged the status quo, built new capabilities, elevated scientific excellence, and transformed Medical Affairs into a recognized industry leader. From Canada to Latin America to Global, the accomplishments I am most proud of were never about programs or processes. They were about people coming together as ONE TEAM, united by a shared commitment to patients, innovation, and excellence. To my incredible teams, THANK YOU. Your passion, resilience, courage, and dedication inspired me every day. It has been an honor to learn from you, lead alongside you, and celebrate all that we achieved together, with countless laughter and fun along the way. To my mentors, leaders, colleagues, and friends, THANK YOU for believing in me, challenging me, supporting me, and helping shape both my career and my character. Your impact will stay with me long after this day. A special THANK YOU to my husband Brian Hardy , and daughters, Courtney Hardy and Melissa Hardy . You have been my constant source of strength, perspective, and inspiration. Thank you for your love, encouragement, and unwavering support through every opportunity and every challenge. While my journey at Astellas is ending, I am embracing this next chapter as a sabbatical. A time for professional and personal renewal, reflection, learning, and growth before deciding what comes next. My commitment to advancing Medical Affairs continues. I look forward to remaining active with the Medical Affairs Professional Society (MAPS) , mentoring current and aspiring leaders, contributing to the continued evolution of our profession, and exploring opportunities to apply my experience in transformation, governance, and strategic leadership through board and advisory roles. Please stay in touch. I look forward to continuing the relationships and conversations that have made my journey so meaningful. THANK YOU for being part of my journey, and for allowing me to be part of yours. #Astellas #Gratitude #Leadership #MedicalAffairs #Transformation #Sabbatical #StayConnected #PatientsFirst**

A sincere thank you to our Chiesi GRD China team for their meticulous organisation, warm hospitality, and unwavering dedication to expanding access for people living with rare diseases across China.
